8d8cf9efc36b92fb: New make spirit Wine and spirits
06ec55107663117a: Clear spirit straight off the still before any cask ageing. Its quality sets the ceiling for the finished whisky. Read the guideAlso: new make
789dcd0a9482c997: Beer served with a nitrogen and CO2 gas mix through a restrictor tap, giving tiny bubbles, a cascading pour and a creamy head. Dry stout is the classic example. Read the guideAlso: nitrogenated beer
bea08685e3d80043: Traditional European aroma varieties, usually Hallertau Mittelfrüh, Tettnang, Spalt and Saaz, prized for soft floral and spicy character. They define classic German and Czech lagers. Read the guide
16bec181094a5900: Packaging line score that multiplies availability, performance and quality into one percentage. It shows how much theoretical output actually becomes good, saleable product. Read the guideAlso: overall equipment effectiveness
f845359e5182f559: Any aroma or taste that does not belong in a beer or its style, caused by faults in ingredients, process, hygiene or packaging. Learning to name them is the core of brewery QC. Read the guideAlso: fault
d41d6998affd4d49: Sales of packaged drinks to take away and drink elsewhere, mainly through licensed liquor shops in India. Rules on who may sell vary by state. Read the guideAlso: off-premise
e0c54e54352839b3: Sales of drinks for consumption where they are bought, such as bars, pubs, restaurants and hotels. Margins and brand building work very differently here than in retail. Read the guideAlso: on-premise
c1ddb45b285e6191: Gravity of wort before fermentation starts, showing how much sugar the yeast has to work with. It largely sets the potential strength of the beer. Read the guideAlso: OG
474a95d42483d89f: Ageing of beer by oxygen, bringing papery, cardboard or sherry flavours while hop aroma fades. Low oxygen pickup with cold storage slows it. Read the guideAlso: Staling
81e5da5c874256e5: Stale flavours of wet cardboard, paper, honey or sherry that develop as beer reacts with oxygen. Hoppy beers also lose their aroma and can turn dull or darker. Read the guideAlso: stale
60e60e9bb020ad59: Oxygen that gets into beer during transfers, centrifuging or packaging. Each step adds a little, so breweries measure before and after each one to find the leak. Read the guide
4d5abeec4eeb24d7: Golden to amber ale of moderate strength with a balance of malt and hops. It is the parent of the IPA and a common flagship for new breweries. Read the guide
bd2cfc18f58db003: Heating beer to kill spoilage microbes and extend shelf life. Flash pasteurisation heats beer in bulk before filling; tunnel pasteurisation heats sealed bottles or cans. Read the guide
08b30dcad2fd483e: Measure of heat dose in pasteurisation: one PU equals one minute at 60 °C (140 °F). Too many units dull flavour, so breweries set a target dose for each beer. Read the guideAlso: PU
06550024079cf4a0: Measure of heat treatment where one unit equals one minute at 60°C (140°F). Breweries target a PU range that kills spoilage organisms without cooking the beer. Read the guideAlso: PU
9642c707efeb2636: Partly decayed vegetation burned to dry malted barley, giving smoky, medicinal flavours measured in phenol parts per million. Islay whiskies are the best-known peated style. Read the guide
b096b8645235f82b: Scale of acidity from 0 to 14, where 7 is neutral and lower numbers are more acidic. Brewers track it at every stage because enzymes, hop bitterness, yeast health and flavour all depend on it. Read the guide
06c84ad2f1d63682: Electronic probe that measures acidity. Brewers check pH in the brewhouse and in finished beer because it affects flavour, stability and microbial safety. Read the guide
cc64dba0d75e3d2f: Clove, smoky, plastic or medicinal flavours from phenol compounds. Expected in hefeweizen and some Belgian ales, they are a fault elsewhere, often from wild yeast or chlorine. Read the guide
9738c55220159b8c: Pale, crisp, hop-accented lager first brewed in Plzen, Bohemia, in 1842. German versions are drier and more bitter; Czech versions are rounder and maltier. Read the guideAlso: Pils, Pilsener
db3c74e7fe717dd7: Very pale base malt kilned at low temperature, giving light colour with a clean, grainy sweetness. It is the standard foundation for pilsner, helles and many pale lagers. Read the guideAlso: Pils malt
f3bb42292d55aa12: Adding yeast to cooled, aerated wort to start fermentation. The amount and health of yeast pitched decide how quickly and cleanly the beer ferments. Read the guide
f23ad37fbbcc4837: Number of yeast cells added per millilitre of wort per degree Plato. Common guides are about 0.75 million cells for ales and 1.5 million for lagers; under-pitching invites off-flavours. Read the guide
288f111cdbb7beb7: Percentage by weight of dissolved extract in wort, so 12 °P means 12 g of extract per 100 g of wort. It is the standard gravity unit in professional brewing. Read the guideAlso: Degrees Plato, °P
854d981cc75fd985: Dark brown ale from 18th-century London with chocolate, caramel and toast flavours, usually softer in roast than stout. The line between the two has always been blurry. Read the guide
19a68dedf31b6731: Copper still run in batches, usually twice for malt whisky, giving a heavier, more flavourful spirit. The copper also strips out sulphur compounds. Read the guide
183b2cb858fa7765: Main fermentation, when yeast consumes most of the sugar, usually lasting a few days to two weeks depending on style and temperature. Most flavour compounds form here. Read the guideAlso: Primary
5dbde7895a75589d: Measured sugar added before bottling or kegging so the remaining yeast produces the right carbonation. Too much can cause gushing or burst bottles. Read the guide
6e71384e6c22c615: Older measure of alcohol strength. US proof is twice the ABV, so 40% ABV is 80 proof; British proof differs, with 100 proof equal to about 57.1% ABV. Read the guideAlso: ABV versus proof
bf7a86d802f24df4: Group of enzymes that break proteins into smaller pieces, including amino acids yeast can use. Most of this work happens during malting rather than in the mash. Read the guideAlso: Proteolytic enzymes
9323bf77b1983169: Rest around 45 to 55 °C (113 to 131 °F) where protein-degrading enzymes work. Useful with undermodified malt, it can thin body and foam with modern malts if overdone. Read the guide
42aadf733d9e8bf7: Fine plastic powder that binds haze-forming polyphenols and is removed with them. Dosed before filtration, it improves haze stability and shelf life. Read the guideAlso: Polyvinylpolypyrrolidone
0df5ab83c3a35eb5: Written contract between a brand owner and a host brewery setting out specifications, testing, sign-off and who pays for failed batches. It prevents arguments when a batch goes wrong. Read the guide
276495e4e7716c3f: Share of extract truly fermented, correcting for alcohol being lighter than water, which flatters hydrometer readings. It is always lower than apparent attenuation, roughly 0.8 times it. Read the guide
5b7bc8d0ca1265a4: Handheld instrument that reads sugar content from how much a drop of liquid bends light. It is quick for wort, but alcohol distorts readings once fermentation starts, so a correction is needed. Read the guide
73289cc5c868c130: Alkalinity left over once calcium and magnesium have offset part of it in the mash. It predicts how a water will shift mash pH, so it shows which beer colours that water suits. Read the guideAlso: RA
d946779248e303e6: Glass bottle collected after use, washed and refilled. Common in Indian mass-market beer, it cuts packaging cost but needs careful inspection for chips, residue and scuffing. Read the guide
934ccfe45e91998f: Adjunct that gives a very light, crisp, dry beer with almost no flavour of its own. Its starch gelatinises at high temperature, so it is usually cooked in a cereal cooker before joining the mash. Read the guideAlso: Broken rice, Rice grits
d5cf498aaf75b494: Water forced through a fine membrane that strips out almost all dissolved minerals. It gives brewers a blank slate to rebuild with salts, useful where borewell water is hard or variable. Read the guideAlso: Reverse osmosis water
be511fae79ddb555: Malt roasted at high temperature to give dark colour plus coffee, chocolate or burnt flavours. Used in small amounts, it defines porters and stouts but brings no usable enzymes. Read the guideAlso: Chocolate malt, Black malt
185c1496dcbcb676: Route to market Business and India
7be713079232ad63: Path a product takes from brewery to drinker through depots, distributors, wholesalers and retailers. In India state rules often decide who may buy from whom. Read the guide
6984455da5d76b69: Main conversion rest, usually 62 to 72 °C (144 to 162 °F), where amylases turn starch into sugars. Lower temperatures make a more fermentable wort, higher ones a fuller-bodied beer. Read the guideAlso: Conversion rest
445f229e4cd679a8: Dry, spicy, highly carbonated Belgian farmhouse ale with peppery and fruity yeast character. It was originally brewed for seasonal farm workers in Wallonia. Read the guideAlso: farmhouse ale
e688904109db3280: Reducing microbes on an already clean surface to a safe level with chemicals such as peracetic acid or with hot water. Sanitising a dirty surface does little because soil shields bacteria. Read the guide
59bd662383e78f8e: Trained group of tasters who assess beer by agreed methods, checking flavour, faults and trueness to brand. Their scores are QC data, just like lab numbers. Read the guide
148b9790c2469825: Temperature at which a beer shows its best. Light lagers suit about 3 to 5°C (37 to 41°F), while strong dark ales open up nearer 10 to 13°C (50 to 55°F). Read the guide
ad9eb62327031d02: Lower-alcohol beer, usually under about 5% ABV, built so several can be enjoyed in one sitting. A good one still needs flavour and balance. Read the guide
7167cbcc6f3403e5: How long a packaged beer stays within its intended flavour, set by the brewery from forced ageing and real-time tasting. Heat in Indian supply chains can shorten it sharply. Read the guide
3c8ebe2d53de153e: Volume a brewery sends to distributors or depots, recorded at the factory gate. Shipments can rise while real consumer sales fall, so they are read alongside depletions. Read the guide
99f33b48c5dd04e9: Whisky made only from malted barley at a single distillery. Scotch single malt must also be distilled in pot stills and aged at least three years in oak. Read the guide
c4c51ff39f22d182: Pungent smell like a skunk, burnt rubber or cannabis from 3-MBT, a sulphur compound formed when light hits hop compounds. Brown glass and cans prevent it. Read the guideAlso: 3-MBT
c0a0cc6e6e73470e: Fractional blending system of barrel tiers used for sherry, where wine for bottling comes from the oldest tier and is topped up from younger ones. Each bottle holds a little very old wine. Read the guide
5e1acbfb01520349: Any beer with deliberate tartness from lactic or acetic acid, made with bacteria such as Lactobacillus or Pediococcus or by blending. Methods range from quick kettle souring to years in barrels. Read the guide
8375db4d0de690f2: Unwanted sourness from lactic or acetic acid bacteria, often with haze, ropiness or vinegar notes. It usually traces back to a hygiene gap in hoses, heat exchangers or packaging. Read the guide
74783e79694a1870: Rinsing the grain bed with hot water, usually around 75 to 78 °C (167 to 172 °F), to wash out remaining sugar. Over-sparging pulls tannins once runnings get thin and pH rises. Read the guideAlso: Sparge
e61769acf2eeb5e2: Any malt used in small amounts for colour, flavour or body rather than fermentable extract, including crystal, roasted and smoked malts. Most have little or no enzyme power. Read the guideAlso: Specialty malt
a53b6ba2ed252601: Density of wort or beer relative to water, which reads 1.000. A 12 °P wort is about 1.048; brewers use it to track fermentation and work out alcohol. Read the guideAlso: SG
704600fe7adc8c31: Lab instrument that measures how much light a sample absorbs at a set wavelength. Breweries use it for colour, bitterness units and other standard methods. Read the guide
2fe4bda9cbbdd566: Wet husks and grain residue left after lautering. It is usually sold or given away as cattle feed. Read the guideAlso: Brewers' grains
c59f406e266be35b: Closing a fermenter near the end of fermentation so its own CO2 builds pressure and carbonates the beer. A spunding valve releases gas above the set pressure. Read the guideAlso: Spunding valve
e47625b7092dbc94: American scale for beer colour, measured from light absorbance at 430 nm. Pale lagers sit around 2 to 4 while stouts reach 40 or more. Read the guideAlso: Standard Reference Method
4adf146db1c84378: Gene that lets some yeast make glucoamylase, an enzyme that breaks down dextrins most brewing yeast cannot ferment. STA1-positive strains over-attenuate and are a gushing risk if they reach packaged beer. Read the guideAlso: STA1 gene
44b4e93379297ccb: Slow loss of fresh character as beer ages, driven by oxygen, heat and time. Hop aroma fades first; papery, honey or sherry notes follow. Read the guide
4098e7a09546a2ca: Stage when yeast stops multiplying as sugar runs low and begins to settle. It is also when yeast reabsorbs diacetyl and acetaldehyde. Read the guide
c6802580d9cedfb4: Mash raised through several temperature rests, for example a protein rest, saccharification rests and mash out. It helps with undermodified malts or grists high in adjuncts. Read the guideAlso: Step mashing, Temperature-programmed mash
ec0893c4189de404: Dark, roasty ale made with roasted barley or dark malts, with coffee and dark chocolate flavours. Styles range from dry Irish stout to sweet milk stout and strong imperial versions. Read the guide
e767b948b7e64200: Fermentation that stops before reaching the expected final gravity. Common causes are under-pitching, too little oxygen, a sudden temperature drop or a poorly fermentable wort. Read the guide
d2512a0bf4904dec: Mash or lauter that stops draining because the grain bed has compacted or clogged. Too fine a crush, sticky grains and drawing wort off too fast are common causes. Read the guideAlso: Set mash
57d7f7bb067ad6e9: Balance between sulphate, which sharpens hop bitterness and dryness, against chloride, which rounds out malt and body. Ratios above 2:1 lean hoppy while ratios below 1:1 lean malty. Read the guideAlso: SO4:Cl ratio
77d1839b6918ac2c: Sulphur dioxide added to wine to protect it from oxidation and spoilage microbes. Most wines contain some, which is why many markets require a sulphite warning on the label. Read the guideAlso: SO2, sulphur dioxide
61a4f745d0eba2d9: Rotten egg or struck match aroma from hydrogen sulphide and related compounds made by yeast. A trace in young lager often fades with conditioning; persistent sulphur suggests stressed yeast. Read the guideAlso: H2S
7bc6ae250b6f5b9f: Polyphenols from grape skins, seeds, stems and oak that give red wine its drying grip. Tannin softens with age and helps a wine last. Read the guide
2ea006eb7e76a5e9: Astringent compounds from husks and hops. Over-sparging, hot or alkaline sparge water and a very fine crush extract more of them, giving a harsh, drying finish. Read the guideAlso: Polyphenols
456f0a3e718b7959: Bar attached to a production brewery where its own beer is poured fresh. It earns the full retail margin and builds the brand directly with drinkers. Read the guide
546dcb38b61d6a65: Combined effect of site, soil, climate and slope on the character of a wine. It explains why the same grape tastes different from different vineyards. Read the guide
17d05de71fce8809: Sulphur compounds giving intense tropical, passion fruit and grapefruit aromas at extremely low concentrations. Much of their potential sits locked in bound forms that certain yeasts can release. Read the guide
f9d4b766af82de2c: Total package oxygen Packaging and quality
105f1d18971dc2f4: All the oxygen in a sealed package: the dissolved oxygen in the beer plus the oxygen in the headspace. It is the figure that best predicts how fast a packaged beer will stale. Read the guideAlso: TPO
d0621d8399a3bb56: Sparkling wine method where a second fermentation happens in the bottle, followed by ageing on lees, riddling and disgorging. Champagne is made this way. Read the guideAlso: méthode traditionnelle
57127f774ef9e163: Document issued by the state excise department to move alcohol from a brewery to a warehouse, retailer or another state. Requirements and processes vary by state. Read the guideAlso: excise pass
8bd82008d391d725: Sensory test where tasters get three samples, two identical and one different, then must pick the odd one. It shows whether a process change makes a detectable difference. Read the guide
a58fb752b5fd80d8: Sediment of coagulated protein, hop debris and fats left after the boil or at the bottom of a fermenter. Separating it gives a cleaner fermentation. Read the guide
f34f4447151f8c01: True to type Packaging and quality
60ee9c52d40670b9: Sensory check of whether a batch tastes as the brand should, judged against a fresh reference sample. It catches drift that lab numbers alone can miss. Read the guideAlso: TTT
a477d8c52f996f82: Long machine that sprays filled bottles or cans with water in warming, holding and cooling zones as they travel through. It treats the beer inside the sealed pack. Read the guide
e3db9eadc9707625: Pressure-rated cylindroconical tank that can ferment, condition and carbonate beer in one vessel. Its cone lets yeast be dumped or harvested, saving transfers and oxygen pickup. Read the guide
c124d9cbf85d82bb: Gin method where botanicals sit in a basket above the boiling spirit so the rising vapour extracts their aroma. It gives a lighter, more delicate result than soaking the botanicals in the spirit. Read the guide
0466454d37b7fd35: Diacetyl plus 2,3-pentanedione, measured together in the lab. Many breweries cool a beer only once VDK falls below their set limit. Read the guideAlso: Vicinal diketones
8da46f4d908fb0ca: Percentage of yeast cells in a slurry or pack that are alive, usually checked with a stain such as methylene blue under a microscope. It decides how much yeast you actually need to pitch. Read the guideAlso: Yeast viability
1356d1afd796bb42: Year the grapes were harvested, printed on many wine labels. Weather that year shapes quality, so vintage matters most in marginal climates. Read the guide
7a9f410bd8b8c776: Metabolic fitness of living yeast cells, or how ready they are to ferment strongly. Viable but stressed yeast can still give a slow start and off-flavours. Read the guideAlso: Yeast vitality
7bf37aa207e142ca: Volumes of CO2 Fermentation and conditioning
35e7f33be9a887b7: Unit of carbonation where one volume means the beer holds its own volume of CO2 at standard temperature and pressure. Most lagers sit around 2.5 to 2.8 volumes, British cask ales much lower. Read the guideAlso: Vols
de30edb882c10952: Recirculating the first cloudy runnings back over the grain bed until the wort runs clear. It sets the filter bed before collection into the kettle starts. Read the guideAlso: Recirculation
9e82f3acb23689af: Fermented liquid, much like an unhopped beer, that a distiller feeds into the still. For malt whisky it is usually around 7 to 9% ABV. Read the guide
2da3c232b94f2911: West Coast IPA Tasting and styles
b5a338b3b28c52fc: American IPA that is clear, dry and assertively bitter, with piney, resinous and citrus hop character. It grew up in California and the Pacific Northwest. Read the guide
aeca3824fb7ed128: Beer brewed with a large share of wheat, often half the grist or more, giving a soft body and good foam. Styles include hefeweizen, witbier and American wheat. Read the guide
cbb4ea8862ef081b: Malted wheat, which has no husk and carries more protein than barley malt. It boosts foam and body, making it essential in hefeweizen and common in other wheat beers. Read the guide
853df456fb7ced51: Swirling hot wort after the boil so trub and hop debris collect in a cone at the centre of the vessel. Brewers also add whirlpool hops here for aroma. Read the guide
89a478d0fa8aa6ba: Dried hop cones left otherwise unprocessed. They are bulky and oxidise faster than pellets, yet some brewers prefer their gentler aroma and they work as a filter bed in a hop back. Read the guideAlso: Leaf hops, Whole hops
65a378f38ab330e0: Sweet liquid drained from the mash that becomes beer once it is boiled, hopped and fermented. Pronounced 'wurt', it is the brewer's main product until the yeast goes in. Read the guide
9f23b8f29ebdfd0a: Adding oxygen to cooled wort so yeast can build healthy cell membranes. It is the only point in brewing where oxygen is wanted; later it causes staling. Read the guideAlso: Oxygenation
